run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-15T08:09:03Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The frontend RequestErrorRate alert is explained by failures on the cart service's call path, whose own error spans begin at the same time. The deepest supported cause is the valkey-cart pod, the cart service's Redis/Valkey backend: the pod is Running but its container is not ready, in CrashLoopBackOff with restartCount 4, last termination reason OOMKilled (exit code 137, finishedAt 08:12:02Z), under a container memory limit of only 10Mi. The valkey-cart Deployment has spec.replicas=1 but no readyReplicas/availableReplicas, and the cart service's own container logs repeat "Wasn't able to connect to redis" from 08:10:24Z onward. frontend error spans are on cart/checkout operations (GET /api/cart, POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout and the grpc CartService/CheckoutService client spans); frontend's client spans to product-catalog, ad and recommendation show no error increase. checkout's errors are on its cart client spans and its own PlaceOrder span. Jaeger returned no incident-window spans (its in-memory sample only covers 07:48Z), so error detail tags for the failing spans are unavailable, and change history is not integrated, so when the 10Mi limit was set, or whether valkey memory merely grew into it, is unknown.

claims.text: frontend STATUS_CODE_ERROR span counts (10m increase) were 0 up to the 08:04:03Z point, then 8.42 at 08:09:03Z, 429.47 at 08:14:03Z, 816.91 at 08:19:03Z and 377.47 at 08:24:03Z; the error series for span ops GET, GET /api/cart, POST, POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout, executing api route (pages) /api/cart, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder rise together from the 08:09:03Z point.

In the same frontend query the client spans to other dependencies show no error increase at any point in the window: grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations and GET /api/data all stay at 0 STATUS_CODE_ERROR while those operations keep serving STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans (e.g. ProductCatalogService/GetProduct 1260.76 per 10m at the 08:24:03Z point).

Frontend error spans first appear at the 08:09:00Z 2m point (GET 2, GET /api/cart 2, POST 2, POST /api/cart 2, CartService/AddItem 2, CartService/GetCart 2 per 2m) and grow to tens per 2m by 08:19-08:24Z; POST /api/checkout and CheckoutService/PlaceOrder errors start later, at the 08:13:00Z point.

At 08:24:00Z the span error ratio was cart 0.1180, frontend-proxy 0.0771, frontend 0.0472 and checkout 0.0425 (error spans divided by all spans of the service over 10m; span counts, not request counts).

The cart service's own error spans start at the 08:10:00Z 2m point (POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 2, POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 5.43) and climb to 60-62 per 2m around 08:19-08:20Z; the failing operations are the cart server spans GetCart, AddItem and (small counts) EmptyCart.

checkout's error spans are on its client span to cart (oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, oteldemo.CartService/EmptyCart) and its own server span oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (e.g. 9.08, 31.90, 15.10 per 10m at the 08:14, 08:19 and 08:24 points) - the cart dependency edge is visible in checkout's own spans.

Pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft (namespace otel-demo, owned by ReplicaSet valkey-cart-58df56c79c) is phase Running but container valkey-cart is ready=false, restartCount=4, state waiting reason CrashLoopBackOff, and lastState.terminated reason OOMKilled with exitCode 137, startedAt 08:11:51Z / finishedAt 08:12:02Z.

The valkey-cart container's resource limits are memory 10Mi and cpu 10m (requests memory 4Mi, cpu 2m) with image valkey/valkey:8.1.3-alpine; the pod cgroup's container_memory_max_usage_bytes for valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft is 10493952 bytes in the single sample available at 08:28:00Z, i.e. at/above the 10485760-byte (10Mi) limit, while the individual valkey container instances report max usage of 2637824-5582848 bytes.

Deployment valkey-cart has spec.replicas=1 but status.readyReplicas and status.availableReplicas are absent (no ready replica), with container limits memory 10Mi / cpu 10m, whereas the cart, checkout and frontend deployments each show ready=1 and available=1.

Pod cart-755465879b-4p8d9 is Running and ready with restartCount 0 (container started 07:31:36Z) and its container logs repeat the exact line "Wasn't able to connect to redis" from 08:10:24Z, with a brief "Connection to redis was restored successfully." at 08:10:26Z and then continuous failures from 08:11:04Z through 08:16:26Z (324 matching lines, 60 newest shown).

Namespace events show the valkey-cart container being Created and Started at 08:13:35Z/08:13:37Z and a Warning BackOff at 08:16:19Z for restarting failed container valkey-cart in pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft, consistent with the CrashLoopBackOff state; no Evicted event and no OOMKilling event text was returned for the pod.

Other pods in otel-demo are Running and ready with restartCount 0 (including cart, checkout, frontend, frontend-proxy, product-catalog, currency, payment, shipping, email, accounting, quote, ad, recommendation, fraud-detection and kafka); valkey-cart is the only pod with a non-true ready state, a waiting reason and a non-zero restart count.

Error-labelled trace series exist and stay at 0 throughout the window for accounting and payment (0 at every point 07:49-08:24Z); ad, recommendation and fraud-detection show a small pre-existing error increase already present at 07:54Z (about 1.05 per 10m, fraud-detection 1.26 by 08:24Z) that does not follow the 08:09Z step change seen in frontend/cart/checkout.

The Jaeger sample for frontend returned spans only from 07:48:03-07:48:04Z (before the incident) and every one of them carries success statuses (http.status_code 200 on frontend/frontend-proxy/load-generator spans, rpc.grpc.status_code 0 on cart, product-catalog and recommendation spans), including the HGET/HMSET/EXPIRE spans of cart; spans_shown 102 with incomplete_reason that the backend returned as many traces as requested.

Primary cause chain: valkey-cart, the Redis backing store of the cart service, runs with a 10Mi memory limit; the container exceeded that limit and was OOMKilled (exit 137) and is now in CrashLoopBackOff with no ready replica in its Deployment, so cart cannot connect to redis ("Wasn't able to connect to redis") and its GetCart/AddItem/EmptyCart server spans return errors, which surface as error server spans on frontend /api/cart and /api/checkout, driving the frontend RequestErrorRate alert. checkout and frontend-proxy errors are on the same cart-dependent paths.

Secondary, unresolved candidate: the memory pressure may come from valkey data growth under the cart workload rather than from a configuration change. Only one cadvisor sample exists (08:28:00Z) and there is no memory time series in the window to show growth, and change history is not integrated, so this remains an open alternative explanation for why the 10Mi limit was exceeded.

Rejected as the cause: the cart workload itself restarting or being rolled out. The running cart pod cart-755465879b-4p8d9 is ready with restartCount 0 and has been running since 07:31:36Z, and the 08:06:51-08:06:52Z Killing/FailedKillPod events concern a different pod, cart-9fd895bb7-m7zfz, which is not owned by the current cart ReplicaSet cart-755465879b (created 07:31:23Z); no cart application startup or crash error appears in its logs, which instead show redis connectivity failures.

Against a broader platform fault: every other otel-demo pod is Running and ready with restartCount 0, and the frontend's non-cart dependencies keep serving: frontend client spans to ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, AdService/GetAds and RecommendationService/ListRecommendations carry no STATUS_CODE_ERROR increase while the same window shows large UNSET counts for them.

Raise the valkey-cart container memory limit (currently 10Mi, request 4Mi) in the valkey-cart Deployment to a realistic value for Valkey and confirm the pod becomes ready and leaves CrashLoopBackOff; then verify the valkey-cart Deployment reports a ready/available replica and that cart's "Wasn't able to connect to redis" lines stop.

Review the deployment/change record for valkey-cart (limits and data volume) to determine whether the 10Mi limit is a recent change or the data set grew into it, and add memory-usage alerting for the pod, since the only cadvisor memory sample retained was at 08:28:00Z.

gaps: list_prometheus_rules returned no rule named RequestErrorRate (view 451f5fde-fc7f-4aa3-98e6-8779d71dde1f-t0:bbe3b098-b909-4708-999f-23aa3eae4223, status no_data), so the alert's exact expression and the value 3.0222 quoted in the alert annotation could not be reproduced or verified against a rule definition.

No change-history integration is available, so it is unknown whether the valkey-cart 10Mi memory limit or its data volume changed before 08:08Z; the current valkey-cart ReplicaSet was created 07:31:23Z, which is the only deployment timing evidence available.

The valkey-cart container log read returned no lines (view 0e6ec1cd-1934-413a-b8b3-76782065b328-t0:37855987-9cbd-4a1f-a7cd-cb8748811e2f, status no_data, no previous container instance), so valkey's own OOM/startup output could not be read.

A frontend pod log read for 08:09-08:20Z returned no lines (view 8dbba68d-b253-43b9-81a3-51f0d960ce8a-t1:d99c30b0-3fd6-49d2-b592-7a3d89897081, status no_data), so the frontend's own application-level error/5xx log lines are unknown.

Jaeger's in-memory store returned only frontend traces from 07:48:03-07:48:04Z (view a9324480-0122-4791-ac21-42f1275b167d-t0:f278744a-3aad-4502-a0a4-56eecd48735c, incomplete) and a traces_search for 08:14-08:20Z returned no_data (view 96b21b0a-eba6-4516-8e42-1a9e9ba810b6-t1:4dd63691-c9b7-42f4-91df-036c6d28b620), and a tag-filtered error search for cart returned no_data (view 676cb6ee-159e-4e6b-a4ee-651cc6e10065-t0:b5dfdb55-fb91-41c3-871d-eb763378e83a); error detail fields, gRPC status codes and HTTP 5xx codes for the failing cart/frontend spans in the incident window are therefore unknown.

The times of valkey-cart's first three container restarts and any earlier OOM are unknown: only lastState (OOMKilled, 08:11:51-08:12:02Z) and restartCount 4 are exposed, and no earlier OOMKilling/Killing events for that pod were returned.

Prometheus holds only a single cadvisor sample (08:28:00Z) for the valkey-cart containers, so no memory growth trend can be shown, and container_memory_failcnt reads 0 only at that one sample (view 6897332b-d833-4c5a-8ea6-b430e0ca4316-t1:bfef6b98-7998-496a-a188-bc70dc677b8a).
No kube_* kube-state-metrics series were returned by metric discovery (only container_* series), so deployment/replicaset history is limited to the current objects.

An http_server_request_duration_seconds_count lookup returned no_data both for label values and for all labels (views 69575c49-f565-4cbf-bcf3-2cac5b4c6b5c-t0:c6f49ff3-9b4e-4486-84f1-258829b3f1ec and a9324480-0122-4791-ac21-42f1275b167d-t1:8f28057a-c9ce-4f7c-b213-cfb8261d40ea), so HTTP status-code-level error rates for frontend are unavailable and the alert's own metric could not be inspected.

Error series were not returned at all for currency, email, image-provider, product-catalog, quote and shipping, so their error state in this window is unknown rather than zero; cart's own error series also only begins at the 08:09:03Z sample, so cart's error behaviour before that instant is unknown.

The reason for the 08:06:51-08:06:52Z FailedKillPod/Killing events on the stale pod cart-9fd895bb7-m7zfz (absent from the current pod and ReplicaSet lists) could not be determined; its events overlap the incident start but nothing ties it to the redis failures.
next_steps: Check the GitOps/change record for the valkey-cart Deployment memory limit and for any recent cart data-volume change, since change history is not integrated here.
After the limit is corrected, confirm the valkey-cart Deployment reports a ready replica and that cart's redis connection log lines stop before declaring the incident resolved.
Add memory-usage alerting for valkey-cart and retain container memory history, since the available cadvisor data was a single sample and could not show the growth that drove the OOM.
